calls.head: The Flyers roll four lines, the Devils lean on their top six
calls.body: On depth, Philadelphia is one of the league’s best, but New Jersey is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Flyers.
calls.call: The Flyers spread their forward ice time deeper down the lineup than the Devils.

surprises.head: Philadelphia couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: New Jersey usually gives up some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Not tonight: Philadelphia’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 4.0% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.3% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 50 games.

story.head: Jack Hughes wins it in overtime
paras: Amadeus Lombardi played his first NHL game. Luke Evangelista made his Devils debut, after four seasons with the Predators, and picked up an assist. Rasmus Ristolainen got the scoring started for the Flyers on the power play midway through the first. Dougie Hamilton made it 1-1 late in the second. Travis Sanheim put the Flyers ahead 2-1 early in the third. Luke Hughes tied it 2-2, 4:11 later. Jack Hughes won it in overtime.

The Devils owned the chances, outshooting the Flyers 44-25, and still had to sweat it out in overtime. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Devils win in regulation about seven in ten. Jake Allen made 23 saves for the Devils, and Joseph Woll stopped 41 of 44. The Devils moved to 1-0-0, and the Flyers fell to 0-1-1.

items.text: The Devils won their home opener.
Both of the preview’s calls held.
